react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on a single biological axis: androgen and estrogen metabolism is the dominant affected pathway across all methods. RaMP multi-DB ORA (merged DB) ranks KEGG:map00150 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' at rank 2 with an FDR of 1.34e-13 and a fold-enrichment of 1429.7, driven by five input steroids (testosterone, 17β-estradiol, estrone, 5α-dihydrotestosterone, DHEA). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently identifies KEGG:hsa00140 (equivalent map) as its top hit with p=8.39e-06, implicating the same five steroids. Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis confirms the same pathway as its top rank (p=8.40e-05) with a striking 13/13 overlap (all 13 pathway members found among the input set), confirming comprehensive coverage of the steroidogenesis network. A secondary but reproducible finding connects tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) and S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (SAH) through tyrosine metabolism (Mummichog rank 3, p=0.027), where BH4 is a co-substrate for aromatic amino acid hydroxylases and SAH is a product of methyltransferase reactions that consume polyamines including spermidine. Spermidine and SAH additionally appear in the 'Urea cycle/amino group metabolism' Mummichog module. The five driver steroids (DHEA, testosterone, estrone, 17β-estradiol, 5α-dihydrotestosterone) span the complete C19/C18 steroid biosynthesis and interconversion grid, suggesting the treatment perturbs the aromatase/17β-HSD/5α-reductase enzymatic node that sits at the intersection of androgen and estrogen arms. BH4 and SAH together implicate a cofactor/methylation dimension that may modulate steroidogenesis enzyme expression through epigenetic or neurotransmitter-dopamine pathways.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on a single dominant signal: steroid hormone metabolism. RaMP multi-DB ORA (merged SMPDB+KEGG+Reactome+WikiPathways) returns SMPDB:SMP00068 "Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism" and KEGG:map00150 (identical label) both at FDR=1.34e-13 as its top two hits, with five input steroids hitting a 27-member roster (fold enrichment=1430). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently identifies KEGG:hsa00140 as its top hit with p=8.391e-06, implicating the same five steroids. Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis confirms MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as its top rank (p=0.00025) with all 13 pathway metabolites matched, and MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism at rank 2. Cross-paradigm consensus identifies dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, estrone, 17β-estradiol, and 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one (dihydrotestosterone) as the driver steroid set driving the primary signal. The three non-steroid inputs map to secondary findings. Tetrahydrobiopterin appears in both MUMM:biopterin_metabolism (rank 5, p=0.059) and MUMM:tyrosine_metabolism (rank 3, p=0.029), the latter also containing SAH. Spermidine and SAH co-enrich in MUMM:urea_cycle_amino_group_metabolism (rank 3, p=0.029), representing a secondary amino-group dimension.

  "narrative_text": "Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on a single biological axis: androgen and estrogen metabolism is the dominant affected pathway across all methods. RaMP multi-DB ORA (merged DB) ranks KEGG:map00150 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' at rank 2 with an FDR of 1.34e-13 and a fold-enrichment of 1429.7, driven by five input steroids (testosterone, 17β-estradiol, estrone, 5α-dihydrotestosterone, DHEA). A secondary but reproducible finding connects tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) and S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (SAH) through tyrosine metabolism (Mummichog rank 3, p=0.027), where BH4 is a co-substrate for aromatic amino acid hydroxylases and SAH is a product of methyltransferase reactions that consume polyamines including spermidine. final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on a single biological axis: androgen and estrogen metabolism is the dominant affected pathway across all methods. RaMP multi-DB ORA (merged DB) ranks KEGG:map00150 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' at rank 2 with an FDR of 1.34e-13 and a fold-enrichment of 1429.7, driven by five input steroids (testosterone, 17β-estradiol, estrone, 5α-dihydrotestosterone, DHEA). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently identifies KEGG:hsa00140 (equivalent map) as its top hit with p=8.39e-06, implicating the same five steroids. Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis confirms the same pathway as its top rank (p=8.40e-05) with a striking 13/13 overlap (all 13 pathway members found among the input set), confirming comprehensive coverage of the steroidogenesis network. A secondary but reproducible finding connects tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) and S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (SAH) through tyrosine metabolism (Mummichog rank 3, p=0.027), where BH4 is a co-substrate for aromatic amino acid hydroxylases and SAH is a product of methyltransferase reactions that consume polyamines including spermidine. Spermidine and SAH additionally appear in the 'Urea cycle/amino group metabolism' Mummichog module. The five driver steroids (DHEA, testosterone, estrone, 17β-estradiol, 5α-dihydrotestosterone) span the complete C19/C18 steroid biosynthesis and interconversion grid, suggesting the treatment perturbs the aromatase/17β-HSD/5α-reductase enzymatic node that sits at the intersection of androgen and estrogen arms. BH4 and SAH together implicate a cofactor/methylation dimension that may modulate steroidogenesis enzyme expression through epigenetic or neurotransmitter-dopamine pathways.
